For pool host cell protein the NOR-propagated PAR reaches the edge of the range studied for protein load, load flow rate and end of pool collect, and no claim is made beyond it. For elution buffer pH it is `{python} hcp_par_nor['elution_ph']`, against `{python} hcp_par_sp['elution_ph']` in the set-point analysis. The lowest elution pH of the range fails when the other parameters move within their NOR, because a single run at high load and low pH can then exceed the criterion. The PAR of elution buffer pH still contains its NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])` with room on both sides. The lack of fit test for this model was close to its limit (@sec-rsm).

For leached Protein A and fragments the table rows come from models that are not adequate, and no PAR is claimed from them. Every run of the designs met these criteria at every corner of the range studied, so neither output constrains any parameter within it.

@fig-par-hcp shows the PAR of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein, the parameter with the largest main effect on it. The left panel shows the set-point analysis and the right panel the NOR-propagated analysis, with the acceptable region shaded green. No PAR figure is shown for leached Protein A or fragments, because no adequate model results for them.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hcp
#| fig-cap: "PAR of elution buffer pH for pool HCP (ng/mg). Left, set-point analysis. Right, NOR-propagated analysis (95 % prediction interval of a single run). Green, the region that meets the criterion."
_fig = D.fig_par(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", gov_hcp)
plt.show()
```

Each PAR holds while the other parameters stay within their NOR, and the design space of @sec-ds describes the joint region. The pool host cell protein PARs come from a scale-down model that is qualified for that output (finding F1), and they are claimed. Operating temperature and bed height have no model-based PAR. Their ranges rest on the measured responses at each end of the range studied, with the other parameters at their set-points (@sec-uni).

# Process capability and robustness

Capability at commercial scale was estimated from the integrated model of the train, with `{python} mc_n` simulated batches and each parameter drawn within its NOR. @tbl-cap gives the drug substance capability of the attributes to which this step contributes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(capd.reset_index())
print()
print(": Commercial-scale capability of the drug substance attributes to which the Protein A step contributes. {#tbl-cap}")
```

Host cell protein has the lowest Cpk of the three, `{python} f2(cpk_hcp)`. PCMP-001 §7.9 expects a Cpk of at least `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` of a CQA in routine manufacture, following common industry practice, and requires an action in the control strategy below `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)`. `{python} 'The target is met for host cell protein and fragments.' if cpk_met else 'The target is not met for every attribute.'` Fragments reach `{python} f2(cpk_frag)`. The Cpk of `{python} f0(cpk_lpa)` for leached Protein A is not meaningful. The simulated drug substance values average `{python} g(lpa_ds_mean)` ppm, `{python} 'below' if lpa_ds_below_loq else 'above'` the limit of quantitation of the ELISA (`{python} g(lpa_loq)` ppm, AMV-3016), so they cannot be measured and their spread is that of the model, not of a result. `{python} 'No simulated batch fell outside these criteria.' if n_oos == 0 else str(n_oos) + ' simulated batches fell outside these criteria.'` These figures describe the drug substance after cation exchange and anion exchange have removed most of what the Protein A pool carries. The lowest Cpk of the drug substance, `{python} f2(V['min_cpk'])` for `{python} min_cpk_attr`, belongs to an attribute this step does not change and is discussed in PCMR-001.

Every output met its criterion across the NOR. Load flow rate is associated with lower step yield. End of pool collect is associated with higher step yield and lower pool host cell protein, and within its NOR the design space changes by a few percent of the plane (@sec-ds).

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. Criterion 8 of PCP-005 §7 adds that an effect is practically relevant for an attribute when the NOR-propagated PAR of the parameter is narrower than its range studied, and that a significant effect whose PAR spans the whole range studied does not by itself make the parameter critical. The classes and the reason for each are the following.

- Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP. It raises pool host cell protein (`{python} f0(cH['A']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range) and interacts with elution pH. It is set by the load volume and the titre, and it is readily controlled within its NOR of `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin.
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a WC-CPP. It has the largest effect on pool host cell protein (`{python} f0(cH['B']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range) and the only one whose NOR-propagated PAR is narrower than its range studied. Buffer pH is controlled at preparation and verified at release. DEV-005-01 shows that a buffer below the NOR can pass release when the pH meter is incorrectly calibrated.
- Load flow rate was classified as a KPP. It lowers step yield at high load (the AC interaction) and has no significant effect on pool host cell protein, leached Protein A or fragments.
- End of pool collect was classified as a KPP. It has the largest effect on step yield. It also has a significant effect on pool host cell protein, `{python} f0(SV['D']['rsm'])` ng/mg across the range studied, and the sign of that effect differs between the designs (finding F10). Its NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein spans the whole range studied. Within its NOR, the design space changes from `{python} f"{ds2_dlo:.0f}"` % of the plane at the low edge to `{python} f"{ds2_dhi:.0f}"` % at the high edge (@sec-ds). The class would be revisited if a later study confirmed the screening sign.
- Operating temperature was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['temperature'])` ng/mg, which would still leave the highest result below the criterion, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni).
- Bed height was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['bed_height'])` ng/mg, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). It is fixed by the packing specification of the commercial column and does not vary in operation. A short bed at the upper end of the load range was not characterized, and no claim is made for it.

In summary the step has `{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs, `{python} n_kpp` KPPs and `{python} n_gpp` GPPs, and `{python} "no CPP" if n_cpp == 0 else f"{n_cpp} CPP"`. The classes of protein load and elution buffer pH rest on the direction and size of their effects, which agree with the platform history and the mechanism. The PAR of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein is narrower than its range studied, and protein load and elution buffer pH together form the boundary of the design space. The KPP classes rest on the direction of the yield effects in both designs and on the mechanism of breakthrough and of peak collection. They do not rest on the step yield model, which is not used under criterion 1 because the scale-down model was not shown equivalent for step yield (finding F1).

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-cs}

The Protein A step contributes to the control strategy in the following ways.

1. Process parameters. Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within their NORs as WC-CPPs. Load flow rate and end of pool collect are controlled within their NORs as KPPs. Movement outside the NOR and within the PARs of @sec-par is assessed under change control.
2. Material controls. Elution buffer is released against its pH specification. DEV-005-01 showed that this release test depends on a correctly calibrated pH meter.
3. Resin and load. Leached Protein A depends on the resin and is expected to depend on protease activity in the load, which rises with the hold of the clarified harvest before capture (@sec-sdm). Resin use, cleaning and sanitization are controlled by SOP-2008, and the hold of the clarified harvest is characterized in PCR-004.
4. Hold. The Protein A eluate may be held at elution pH for up to `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` before viral inactivation.
5. Downstream clearance and release. Host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments are further cleared by cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008), and they are tested at release of the drug substance. Viral clearance is claimed at low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006), anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-009), and not at this step.

The control strategy of the whole train is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The characterization confirms the main effects that the platform history predicted for this step. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and they interact. End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Two results do not follow the expectations. End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein in the response-surface design and raised it, not significantly, in the screening design, for a reason that was not identified. Load flow rate did not raise pool host cell protein as the mechanism predicts.

Confidence in the scale-down model is the weakest point of the study. For leached Protein A the qualification found a consistent difference, which is expected from the longer hold of the manufacturing load before capture and which was accepted. Even scaled by that difference the design results stay far below the criterion. The planned qualification could not demonstrate equivalence for `{python} sdm0_short`, because `{python} dev_005_03_n_planned` scale-down runs could not narrow the interval below the margin (DEV-005-03). A further `{python} dev_005_03_n_supplementary` runs were made, and the margins were kept. With them the model is qualified for pool host cell protein, which is the output that sets the PARs of the step. Step yield misses equivalence by `{python} miss_tab('step_yield')` % of its margin and column efficiency by `{python} miss_tab('plates_per_m')` %, both on the low side. Neither sets a range, and the step yield model is not used for a range or a prediction.

The response-surface model for pool host cell protein meets criteria 2 to 4 of PCP-005 §7, with a lack of fit test close to its limit. It does not meet criterion 5, and no model does. The conclusions on pool host cell protein rest instead on the deletion of single runs, which showed that no run decides them. The Cook's distance limit of 4/n is better suited to a design with low leverage than to a face-centred design with `{python} int(F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['model'].df_model) + 1` terms in `{python} n_rsm` runs. A limit based on the leverage of each run would serve the purpose of the criterion better. The residuals show no trend with the run order of execution (@tbl-resid).

Leached Protein A and fragments gave no adequate model. For both, any effect of the parameters is small against the variation of the runs and the assay. Both met their criteria in every run, so the absence of a model limits what is known about their shape and not whether the step meets them.

The three deviations of the study did not change its conclusions (@sec-dev). The elution buffer of DEV-005-01 was below the NOR but inside the range studied, the leached Protein A result of DEV-005-02 was replaced by a valid re-assay, and DEV-005-03 was resolved by supplementary runs.

The other limitations are those the plan named. Each design used one feed, so the effect of feed quality on the step was not estimated. The univariate studies cannot detect interactions, and a short bed at high load was not characterized. The laboratory column does not reproduce the hold of the manufacturing load, which raises leached Protein A at scale.

# Conclusions

1. The step was characterized under PCP-005 in a screening design, a response-surface design, a univariate study and a hold study.
2. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and it falls as the end of pool collect is extended. Its model meets criteria 2 to 4 of PCP-005 §7, and its conclusions rest on an influence analysis for criterion 5. End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Leached Protein A and fragments met their criteria in every run, and no adequate model results for either.
3. Every output met its intermediate acceptance criterion across the NOR. The NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein spans the range studied for `{python} n_fac - n_hcp_narrow` parameters and is `{python} hcp_par_nor['elution_ph']` for elution buffer pH.
4. With the supplementary runs of DEV-005-03 the scale-down model is qualified for pool host cell protein and peak asymmetry, with an accepted scale effect for leached Protein A (finding F1). Step yield and column efficiency were not shown equivalent, and neither sets a range.
5. Protein load and elution buffer pH are WC-CPPs, load flow rate and end of pool collect are KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height are GPPs. The step has no CPP.
6. No difference from the set-point runs was detected for operating temperature or bed height, and their ranges studied are supported with the other parameters at their set-points.
7. The eluate may be held at elution pH for `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm`.
8. At commercial scale the lowest Cpk among the attributes of this step is `{python} f2(cpk_hcp)`, for host cell protein, against the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` set in PCMP-001.
9. The three deviations were resolved without changing the conclusions. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan {#sec-dev}

The register lists `{python} n_dev` deviations recorded for the studies of the step. All were investigated. Two were retained, and one was resolved by supplementary runs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
```

Beside the recorded deviations, the analysis used two options that PCP-005 provides. The full quadratic model for step yield was replaced by a reduced model (PCP-005 §7, @sec-rsm), and leached Protein A and fragments were reported descriptively (PCP-005 §5.5). The analysis departed from the plan in one place. Criterion 5 of PCP-005 §7 was not met by any model, and the conclusions on pool host cell protein rest on an influence analysis that the plan does not provide for (@sec-resid). No run was lost or invalidated, and no design was repaired or re-executed.

## DEV-005-01. Elution buffer pH below target on a response-surface run

The elution buffer of lot LOT-BUF-5290 was prepared below its target pH and was used on run `{python} dev_run` of the response-surface design, whose design setting for elution buffer pH was `{python} g(dev_ph_design)`. The buffer had passed release on an incorrectly calibrated pH meter. The error was found at a review of the buffer preparation record after the run, and the pH of the lot was `{python} g(dev_005_01_ph_measured)`. This is below the NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])` and inside the range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])`. The investigation found an error at the titration end point during buffer preparation.

At the design settings of run `{python} dev_run` the model predicts a pool host cell protein of `{python} f0(dev_hcp_pred_design)` ng/mg. At the measured pH it predicts `{python} f0(dev_hcp_pred_meas)` ng/mg. The run gave `{python} f0(dev_hcp_obs)` ng/mg, below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg and `{python} 'closer to the prediction at the design setting than to that at the measured pH' if abs(dev_hcp_obs - dev_hcp_pred_design) < abs(dev_hcp_obs - dev_hcp_pred_meas) else 'closer to the prediction at the measured pH than to that at the design setting'`. The result therefore does not show the rise in pool host cell protein that the lower pH would cause, and the run does not distort the model in that direction. The run was analysed at its design setting, so the error in pH enters the model as part of the residual of this run. Its Cook's distance for pool host cell protein is `{python} f2(dev_cook)`, `{python} "above" if dev_cook_over else "below"` the limit of 4/n. `{python} "Deletion of the run, as for every run above the limit, does not change the conclusion for pool host cell protein" if dev_cook_over else "The run does not influence the fit more than the other runs of the design"` (@sec-resid). The run was retained. The release test is the control on which the WC-CPP class of elution buffer pH relies, and here it failed because the meter was incorrectly calibrated. Run `{python} dev_run` carries a footnote in Appendix B.

## DEV-005-03. Scale-down equivalence not demonstrable with the planned set-point runs

PCP-005 Version 2.0 sets an equivalence margin for each output of the scale-down model qualification and plans `{python} dev_005_03_n_planned` set-point runs in the scale-down model. The Version 2.0 re-analysis of the qualification found that, with `{python} dev_005_03_n_planned` runs, the half-width of the 90 % confidence interval alone was larger than the margin for `{python} sdm0_short`. Equivalence could not have been shown for these outputs whatever the means were. @tbl-sdm0 gives the result on the planned runs alone, where `{python} sdm0_n_eq` of the `{python} len(SDM_RESP)` outputs met the criterion. The root cause is a number of replicates too small for the margin the plan set.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sdm0_df.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True, colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * 7))
print()
print(": Scale-down model qualification on the planned set-point runs of S-PA-SDM alone. Abbreviations as in the qualification table of the methods section. {#tbl-sdm0}")
```

In study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} sdm2_win`), `{python} dev_005_03_n_supplementary` supplementary set-point runs were made during INV-001. The margins were not changed, because a criterion changed after the data are seen is the failure that INV-001 investigated. The equivalence test was repeated over all `{python} n_sd_all` scale-down runs (@sec-sdm). The model is now qualified for pool host cell protein and peak asymmetry. Leached Protein A differs by the accepted scale effect. Step yield and column efficiency were not shown equivalent, and neither sets a range. The supplementary runs were made after the characterization studies, so the qualification for pool host cell protein was completed after the data it supports were collected.

## DEV-005-02. Leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` initially out of trend

The leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` of the response-surface design was out of trend at analytical review. The sample was re-assayed under AMV-3016. The investigation attributed the first result to suspected carryover in the ELISA. The re-assay result, `{python} f2(dev02_val)` ppm, is the one reported in Appendix B and used in the analysis, and the first result was kept in the record with its status marked. The re-assay result lies inside the range of the other runs of the design and far below the intermediate acceptance criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm.
